name: Sensa Autoterm Baltica Heater Controller Pro (PoE)
Asustor Flashstor 6
_discovery_note: OUI prefixes UNVERIFIED — Asustor units often carry the NIC vendor's OUI (Realtek/Intel/AQC), so DHCP-OUI discovery is unreliable. Verify against demo hardware before relying on it; static_probe (SSH port 22) is the dependable path. Add the NAS's static IP to static_probe.hosts on the demo network.

http_probe.comment: On a split network the SLZB sits on the IOT VLAN and the box on Main. mDNS does not cross that line, so HA's zeroconf never sees it and `native` alone never lists it. `/ha_info` is the call HA's own smlight integration identifies it with (pysmlight), and these keys under `Info` are the identification. Firmware too old to have `/ha_info`, or with web login turned on, is not claimed.

tcp_subnet.comment: A Dongle-M is a bare serial-over-TCP socket: no mDNS, no HTTP, no HA integration, so an open 6638 is the ONLY signal it gives. The sweep walks the scanned subnet(s) rather than a fixed host list — `static_probe` below pins one address, which finds it on exactly one network. But an open port is NOT identification, so a responder is only claimed when its MAC matches `mac_oui_prefixes` (resolved from the ARP table, then HA's DHCP cache); an unidentifiable one is skipped, because the dev LAN has an unrelated host with 6638 open and it surfaced as a phantom Dongle-M. The simulator prefix is `025e000051`, NOT the bare `025e00` OUI: EVERY Sensa sim shares that OUI and they differ only in the tag byte, so the short prefix claimed any sim with 6638 open. It claimed the SLZB simulator the moment that gained a virtual radio, and because both rows carry the same MAC the Dongle-M row then won the dedup and the SLZB vanished from the picker entirely. See _discover_tcp_subnet.

static_probe.comment: Kept for a Dongle-M pinned at this fixed address on a subnet the sweep is not configured to walk (it takes no MAC and so is the only path that finds one whose MAC we cannot resolve). Fails fast when absent. NB it can duplicate a swept row: this emits discovery_id static-<ip> while the sweep emits dongle_m-<mac>, so the same unit found by both paths appears twice — only possible when this address is inside scan_subnet, which it is not by default.

model_detection.comment: Ruuvi advertises a single format-5 payload across every product variant; the variant has to be deduced from which fields carry sentinel (invalid) values. HA's ruuvitag_ble integration does that decode work and stamps `device.model` once it's seen enough packets — `_async_backfill_native_model` reads that back into our backend so the keys here can substring-match against e.g. 'RuuviTag Pro 4in1'. First key whose lowercase form is found inside the model string wins; falls back to the entry-level `image`.

Model is byte-decoded from manufacturer_data[0xEC88] by the govee_ble PyPI library inside _annotate_govee_model (sensor.py); the resulting string lands on the row as `detected_model`. `_match_model_image` does case-insensitive substring matching against these keys, so listing just the model code (H5074, H5075 …) is enough to catch full `title`s like "Govee H5074". Every Govee sensor shares one product photo (the entry-level `image`), so model_images is empty: we name each model, we do not draw each model. A key here would need its own file in webcards/assets/images, and a key naming a file that is not there beats the generic and 404s to a `?`.

ble.comment: 0x0059 is Nordic Semiconductor's id, shared by many unrelated devices, so the 0xFEE5 service UUID is what identifies a Mopeka (both from HA core's mopeka manifest). The native flow's only field, medium_type, defaults to propane, so the {} probe completes it with no input.

_discovery_note: Foxygen packs carry a Daly BMS. Captured on the bench 2026-10-30 from a Foxygen 105Ah with Bluetooth and heating: no local_name, manufacturer_id 0x0302, payload 0x23 + the pack's own MAC + 'DL'. aiobmsble's daly_bms read it over GATT (4 cells, 13.1 V). 0x0302 is one of Daly's generic ids, so any Daly pack advertising it is offered as Foxygen. The advert names no model, so the model comes from the rated capacity in Daly register 0x0080 (0.1 Ah; the 105Ah answered 1050), read by vendors/bms_ble_daly.py. Only the 105Ah has been read; the 230/300/460 values are assumed to follow the same scheme. The switchable heater is not read or written yet.

model_detection.comment: A MultiPlus-II reaches Sensa two ways: today as a Venus `vebus` sub-device under a Cerbo GX (the picker child image comes from VEBUS_FLAVOURS / SERVICE_IMAGES['vebus'] in vendors/victron_mqtt_services.py, NOT this block — the Cerbo child is matched on the family reported in Venus's ProductName, since an EasyPlus / MultiPlus / MultiPlus-II / Quattro all publish the identical `vebus` service); and in future, standalone over BLE via the VE.Bus Smart Dongle (this entry's `discovery.ble`, currently gated off by `discovery_enabled: false`). This model_detection block is for that future BLE path — model strings carry the DC/AC rating (e.g. 'MultiPlus-II 48/5000'). Map keys are the substring searched inside `device.model` (case-insensitive); first hit wins, else the entry-level `image`. All variants point at the single `victron-multiplus2.webp` until per-model art exists.

name: OBEST Tyre Pressure Sensor
_discovery_note: External cap sensor sold in OBEST kits for the 'DJTPMS' phone app. Passive adverts, never connectable. The manufacturer-data 'company ID' is NOT a company ID: it changes between adverts and is CRC input, so there is nothing stable to key on; `_annotate_tpms_advert` stamps device_subtype 'tpms_djtpms' only when the local name is 'DJTPMS' AND the frame's CRC8 checks. Frame layout and CRC: docs/devices/obest-djtpms.md and vendors/tpms_ble.py.

name: DJI Power Station
_discovery_note: One entry for the whole DJI Power range: every unit answers the same DJI DUML smart-battery records over GATT service 0xA002 (request on c303 write-without-response, reply on c305 notify), and cell count and capacity come from the data rather than from a model table, so a model we have never seen still reads correctly. Matching is therefore DELIBERATELY loose: manufacturer_id 0x08AA (SZ DJI Technology, DJI's own company id) plus a 'Power' name prefix, which no DJI drone advertises. model_detection NAMES the known models by their advert prefix (longest match wins, so Power1000V2 is not downgraded to Power1000); anything unrecognised stays 'DJI Power Station' rather than being mislabelled as a model it is not. Captured on the bench 2026-09-04 from a Power 1000 V2: local_name 'Power1000V2-1001UC', manufacturer payload 97 01 10 + the unit's own MAC, radio OUI 58:8C:81 (Espressif). Which models have actually been read on real hardware is `model_detection.verified`, not this note. Protocol notes and field map: docs/devices/dji-power-1000-v2.md.

model_detection.comment: Advert name is the marketing product name with the spaces removed, then a dash and a per-unit suffix ('Power1000V2-1001UC'); the FCC model numbers (DYM1000V2, DYM2000) follow the same product names. Keys are matched with startswith and the LONGEST match wins. Only the 1000 V2 has a product shot, so every other model falls back to the entry image until its own artwork is added.

http_probe.comment: A Lucky Miner is an ESP32 on a DHCP address behind an Espressif OUI it shares with every other ESP32 on the van (our own relay controllers and Bluetooth proxies included), so neither a MAC prefix nor an open port 80 identifies it. What does is the response: the stock firmware is an AxeOS fork and answers GET /api/system/info with a JSON body carrying the AxeOS key set. The sweep claims a responder only when every key in require_keys is present AND the match values agree, which is a protocol handshake rather than a guess. Our own ESPHome devices 404 this path and are rejected.

static_probe.comment: Fallback for a miner pinned at a fixed address on a subnet the sweep is not configured to walk. Port 80 alone is weak identification, so this path is intentionally empty by default: add the address on a demo network only.

name: Aqara Double Rocker Remote Switch H1

rtsp_probe.comment: Any camera that speaks RTSP, no vendor allowlist yet, so there is no OUI to match and an open port 554 is not identification. The sweep sends an RTSP OPTIONS and claims a responder only when it answers with an RTSP status line (200, or 401 for a camera that wants credentials), which is a protocol handshake rather than a guess. At Pro this is the camera nominated for grey-waste dumping; the Vision tier's recording is the same class.

http_probe.comment: Found by Sensa's own sweep, not HA's zeroconf: Shellys live on the IoT VLAN and mDNS does not cross segments. Every Gen2+ Shelly answers GET /shelly with its own id, mac, model and gen, so the sweep claims a responder only on a listed model. One entry per PRODUCT, keyed on model: the Shelly smoke detector answers the same path and is claimed by shelly_plus_smoke, never here. Model ids from aioshelly const.py; SPSW-204PE16EU read off a customer's Pro 4PM 2026-09-21. HA's shelly integration still owns the entities (local push, no cloud, quality_scale platinum); Sensa creates its entry on add.
